findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file I/O error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a recoverable error to the caller
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))? with a typed error enum

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds console I/O inside data-loading logic that should be pure parsing
findings.failure_mode: side effects leak into pure parsing, making the function non-deterministic in output, untestable in isolation, and impossible to compose without stdout pollution
findings.fix: remove all println! from load_sessions; logging belongs in the shell layer that calls the pure parser, not inside the parsing logic itself

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked index access on a Vec built from split without bounds checks
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero comma-separated fields will panic at runtime with index-out-of-bounds, crashing the process on malformed input
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? to safely destructure the two fields without index bounds access

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked index access on a Vec built from split without bounds checks
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one comma-separated field will panic at runtime with index-out-of-bounds, crashing the process on malformed input
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)? and parse the value_str from the tuple rather than indexing a Vec

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value strings
findings.failure_mode: any non-numeric value in the second CSV field causes a process abort instead of a typed parse error, making the parser unusable on hostile input
findings.fix: use parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) to return a typed error on parse failure, parsing directly to u16 to avoid the subsequent lossy cast

findings.problem: (u32 value) as u16 is a lossy cast that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: any u32 value in range 65536..=4294967295 silently wraps to an incorrect u16, producing invalid domain data without any error signal, silently corrupting records
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow)? or parse directly to u16 via parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid) to get both parse and range validation in one typed step

findings.problem: load_sessions fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), console I/O (println!), parsing, and domain construction into a single function, violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.failure_mode: the function cannot be unit-tested as pure logic, cannot be composed without side effects, and conflates shell concerns (disk access, logging) with pure data loading and transformation
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for the calculation layer, (2) a shell function load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> that reads the file, delegates to parse_line, and handles logging/boundary I/O

findings.problem: Record exposes name: String as a raw primitive with no validation — callers can construct Record with empty names, names containing commas, or any invalid value, bypassing the parse boundary entirely
findings.failure_mode: invalid domain states are representable and constructible directly; no smart constructor or typestate enforces that name is a valid domain value, so every caller must repeat validation or risk corrupt data
findings.fix: make Record private with a smart constructor fn new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, ParseError> that validates name is non-empty and value is in range, or introduce a Name newtype with its own constructor

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates an intermediate Vec<String> for every line, and the outer collect() allocates another Vec<Record> with unbounded growth
findings.failure_mode: malformed input with many lines causes unbounded heap allocation with no capacity cap or fallible reserve; the intermediate Vec<String> per line is wasteful when only two fields are needed
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') for two-field records to avoid per-line Vec allocation; add try_reserve on the outer Vec after validating a max_rows cap; use Vec::new() with try_reserve instead of Vec::with_capacity

findings.problem: No typed error type exists; all fallible operations (I/O, parsing, range validation) would collapse into unwrap() panics with no error taxonomy
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish between file-not-found, malformed CSV, out-of-range numeric, or too-many-rows errors — all surface as panics that crash the process
findings.fix: define an enum LoadError { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid(ParseError), TooMany, Overflow, Allocation } and a ParseError { Invalid, Overflow } with From<std::io::Error> for ergonomic ? propagation

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or latency, and no allocation evidence for unbounded Vec growth
findings.failure_mode: without baseline measurement, allocation patterns and performance characteristics are unknown; unbounded input could cause OOM under load
findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring parse throughput on realistic and hostile input sizes, with allocation profiling to verify bounded behavior

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or latency
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in the parsing path
no command evidence that cargo fmt --check passes
no command evidence that cargo clippy passes with strict gates
no command evidence that cargo test passes
no bounded allocation strategy (try_reserve with domain cap) exists
no second-ring evidence for any performance claim
residual_risk: Strict static review only with no commands executed. The crate contains 10 findings including 9 blockers and 1 warning. All absolute laws are violated: unwrap panics on I/O and parse errors, unchecked indexing on split results, lossy u32-to-u16 cast, hidden println! I/O in parsing logic, no typed error taxonomy, no parse boundary validation on Record, and unbounded intermediate allocations. Without running cargo fmt, cargo clippy with strict flags, and cargo test, residual risk remains high.
